questions.question: Summarize the discussion about the effect of training on different languages
questions.reference_answer: Using multiple languages led to more diversity which potentially hindered the model performance. The professor was skeptical about discussing the results since they had not received any good ones so far.

oracle.answer: The discussion focused on the effects of training neural networks on different languages. Participants noted that removing English from a multi-language training set (two languages) did not significantly harm performance compared to a set with three languages. They suggested that the diversity of the training data rather than the specific languages might be more critical. However, when training on a single language and testing on another, the results were poor, indicating that cross-language training might not improve performance as expected. The team planned to further investigate by testing the same training conditions on other languages.

questions.reference_answer: PhD D explained that the multilingual model, trained on French, Spanish, and English, was trained with higher frame rates. It has slightly poorer results when delta was not used. All in all, the addition of English did not seem to help the model.

questions.question: Summarize the discussion on managing the complexity of the model
questions.reference_answer: The team discussed the size of the neural net, which was just a simple net. At the time, it had 27 outputs, but the professor recommended that they use a larger net, with perhaps more features. They discussed the effect that removing silent frames could have on the model. The professor recommended having a bigger hidden layer, though he did not think that would substantially improve performance. Currently, however, the team was facing computational limitations.

oracle.answer: The discussion on managing the complexity of the model centered around simplifying the classification process by reducing the number of classes from sixty-four to twenty-seven. This approach involved using a single neural network (net) with twenty-seven outputs instead of multiple nets. However, concerns were raised that reducing the information too much might worsen performance. Additionally, the team considered incorporating broader classes alongside detailed features to enhance information retention. They planned to experiment with transforming features together versus separately and discussed the potential benefits and computational advantages of using a smaller, specialized net for tasks like Voice Activity Detection (VAD). The conversation highlighted the balance between model complexity and performance, aiming to optimize the model's efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.

questions.reference_answer: The team was concerned about the availability of computational resources. The Professor informed them that they had received two 550 megahertz processors by IBM. Though, they were originally expecting eight 800 megahertz processors.
